shows.specific_content: A single sentence stating "Expressiveness is central to our technological advantage," with the word "Expressiveness" highlighted in green. Above the text is a simple abstract icon of five horizontal teal lines.
shows.data_points_shown: None. This is a qualitative, conceptual slide.

records.abstract_pattern: This pattern introduces a unique, proprietary, or uniquely-defined concept as the cornerstone of a company's competitive advantage. It acts as a 'thesis statement' or a 'chapter header' for a section of the presentation. It uses a single, memorable keyword to encapsulate a complex idea, making it easier for the audience to grasp and recall the source of the company's moat. This pattern is used to frame subsequent slides, which will then provide evidence and examples to support this central claim.
works_for: Our 'Composable Architecture' is the key to our platform's flexibility.
Our 'Intent Graph' is the foundation of our superior personalization.
'Radical Simplicity' is our core design principle and our main differentiator.
Our 'Trust Algorithm' is why we are the most reliable source in the market.
The 'Flywheel Effect' is central to our platform's defensibility.
'Predictive Caching' is the secret to our industry-leading performance.
Our 'Federated Learning' model provides insights no competitor can match.
Our 'Dynamic Pricing Engine' is our core economic advantage.

variable_elements.primary_metric: A proprietary concept or keyword (e.g., 'Expressiveness', 'Intent Graph', 'Composable Architecture').
variable_elements.comparison_basis: Implicitly vs. competitors who lack this core capability.

must_have: A well-defined core concept or term that encapsulates the company's unique advantage.
Supporting proof points for the concept on subsequent slides.
data_requirements.data_shape_needed: Not applicable. This is a conceptual claim, not a data visualization.
data_requirements.minimum_data_points: One core concept.

ideal_for: Introducing the 'secret sauce' or technological moat of your product.
As a title slide for the 'Product' or 'Technology' section of a pitch deck.
When you need to simplify a complex technical advantage into a single, memorable idea.
To frame the narrative before diving into specific product features or proof points.
When your advantage isn't a single feature but a fundamental architectural or philosophical approach.
avoid_when: If you cannot clearly define and prove the concept you're introducing on subsequent slides.
If your advantage is easily replicable or not truly unique (it will sound like empty jargon).
If you are in the very early stages and haven't fully developed your core technology yet.

records.title: Expressiveness is central to our technological advantage.

records.core_message: Our underlying technology ('Bid Factors') is fundamentally different and superior to the industry standard ('Line Items'), enabling greater granularity, optimization, and performance for our customers.

shows.specific_content: A side-by-side comparison of 'Line Items' (the industry standard) and 'Bid Factors' (The Trade Desk's approach). 'Line Items' are depicted as simple, rigid horizontal lines with text describing their limitations. 'Bid Factors' are shown as complex, dynamic, multi-layered line graphs with text highlighting their superior expressiveness and fine-grained reporting capabilities.
shows.data_points_shown: No quantitative data is shown. The slide compares two conceptual models: 'Line Items' (limits granularity, optimization, data activation) vs. 'Bid Factors' (allows expressiveness, fine-grain reporting).

records.abstract_pattern: Any company can use this pattern to explain a core architectural or methodological differentiation that creates a competitive moat. It visually and textually contrasts a simplistic, limited legacy approach with a complex, powerful, modern approach. The slide frames the legacy way as the industry standard and positions the company's unique method as the only way to achieve superior outcomes, directly linking the technical difference to customer value.
works_for: Our event-driven architecture is superior to traditional batch processing for real-time analytics.
Our federated learning model protects user privacy, unlike competitors' centralized data collection.
Our direct-to-consumer supply chain eliminates middlemen, providing better value than the traditional retail model.
Our composable commerce platform offers more flexibility than monolithic legacy suites.
Our novel drug delivery mechanism provides targeted therapy, unlike systemic treatments with broad side effects.
Our decentralized identity system gives users control, contrasting with centralized identity providers.
Our full-stack solution provides seamless integration, unlike the fragmented point solutions used by competitors.

variable_elements.primary_metric: Our unique approach/technology (e.g., Bid Factors, Event-Driven Architecture)
variable_elements.secondary_metric: The inferior industry-standard approach (e.g., Line Items, Batch Processing)
variable_elements.comparison_basis: Our unique methodology vs. the industry standard/competitors' methodology

must_have: A clear definition of the company's unique technical/architectural approach
A clear definition of the contrasting industry-standard/legacy approach
A list of benefits derived from the unique approach
A list of limitations of the standard approach
data_requirements.data_shape_needed: needs a clear conceptual dichotomy (e.g., good vs. bad, new vs. old, flexible vs. rigid)
data_requirements.minimum_data_points: Two contrasting concepts with 2-3 supporting benefit/limitation points for each.

ideal_for: Explaining a fundamental, hard-to-replicate technical advantage.
Justifying why your product delivers superior results (e.g., better ROI, more granularity).
Creating a 'category of one' narrative by defining the old way vs. your new way.
Educating a sophisticated audience about your core innovation.
Answering the question 'How are you different?' at a deep, structural level.
When your moat is based on 'how' you do something, not just 'what' you do.
avoid_when: Your differentiation is based on surface-level features, not fundamental architecture.
The audience is non-technical and won't grasp the conceptual difference.
The difference is minor or easily replicable by competitors.

records.title: We're Built Differently Than Everyone Else in the Industry.

records.core_message: Our platform provides unparalleled transparency and detailed reporting, empowering users with the granular data needed to make sophisticated, data-driven decisions.

shows.specific_content: A screenshot of a software interface, mocked up on a laptop, showing a detailed advertising campaign report. The report is a data table segmented by 'Frequency' and includes numerous columns such as Impressions Bid On, Impressions Won, Win Rate, CPM, Cost in USD, Clicks, Conversions (Post Click/View), eCPC, and CTR.
shows.data_points_shown: The table shows data for ad frequencies 0, 1, and 2. For example, for frequency 1, there were 8.1M impressions bid on, a 28.3% win rate, and a $6.81 CPM. The grand total shows over 105M impressions bid on, resulting in over 12M impressions won at a total cost of ~$69k.

records.abstract_pattern: This pattern uses a direct screenshot of a complex data table or report from the product to visually prove a claim about its sophistication, transparency, or depth. It moves from a high-level benefit statement (e.g., 'Transparent Reporting') to a tangible, 'peek-behind-the-curtain' proof point. Any company can use this to substantiate a technical or data-related competitive advantage, building trust by showing the raw capability rather than just describing it. It's a powerful 'show, don't tell' technique for demonstrating product superiority.
works_for: Our security platform provides the most detailed threat analysis in the industry.
We give supply chain managers unprecedented visibility into every step of their logistics.
Our genomics platform allows researchers to analyze data at the single-cell level.
We offer the most granular attribution modeling for mobile marketing.
Our financial analytics tool provides complete, auditable data lineage for every calculation.
Our CRM provides a truly 360-degree view of the customer with all data sources unified.
Our observability platform lets engineers drill down from a system-level alert to the exact line of code.

variable_elements.primary_metric: Data granularity / Reporting detail
variable_elements.secondary_metric: High-level benefit claim (e.g., Transparency, Power, Control)
variable_elements.comparison_basis: Implicitly vs. competitors (who are presumed to be less transparent or detailed)

must_have: A real or realistic screenshot of a product's detailed data output (e.g., report, dashboard, log).
A key product claim that is visually substantiated by the screenshot (e.g., transparency, detail, power).
data_requirements.data_shape_needed: needs high information density
data_requirements.minimum_data_points: A table or report with at least 5+ columns and 3+ rows to appear sufficiently complex and detailed.

ideal_for: When you need to prove a product's technical depth or sophistication.
To build trust by demonstrating transparency, especially in an opaque market.
To visually substantiate a key competitive differentiator related to data or analytics.
When addressing a sophisticated audience (e.g., power users, technical buyers) who value granular control.
To move beyond marketing claims and show tangible proof of product value.
When your UI, despite its power, is clean enough to be presented as a 'Simplified User Interface'.
avoid_when: Your product's key value is extreme simplicity, and a complex table would be counterproductive.
Presenting to a non-technical audience that would be overwhelmed by the detail.
Your reporting capabilities are not a core differentiator and are merely table stakes.

records.title: Goal: The most transparent and most detailed reporting.

records.core_message: Our platform's sophisticated, multi-dimensional targeting capabilities (e.g., by location and time) allow for highly expressive and optimized campaigns, which directly translates to superior client outcomes like significant cost reduction.

shows.specific_content: A slide with two visuals illustrating advertising bid logic. On the left, a map shows geo-fenced bidding rules (e.g., 1.75x bid within 5 miles of a store). On the right, a bar chart shows a 'Bid Multiplier' decaying over 'Time since last site visit'. The headline claims a 50% cost reduction, and a footer quantifies the platform's capability as '15,360 Bid Permutations'.

records.abstract_pattern: This pattern demonstrates a system's sophistication and technical moat by illustrating how it combines multiple, independent variables to create a highly optimized output. It uses concrete examples of rule-based logic (e.g., one based on geography, another on time) to make the abstract concept of 'power' tangible. The pattern culminates in a large, impressive number representing the total combinatorial possibilities, quantifying the system's 'expressiveness' and justifying its superior performance.
works_for: Our fraud detection engine analyzes 500+ signals in real-time to block sophisticated attacks.
Our supply chain software optimizes routes across weather, traffic, and fuel costs, creating millions of possibilities.
Our personalization engine combines user behavior and real-time context to deliver uniquely tailored experiences.
Our dynamic pricing model adjusts for seasonality, competitor pricing, and inventory levels in real-time.
Our drug discovery platform models molecular interactions across thousands of variables to predict efficacy.
Our marketing automation platform allows for complex user journeys based on dozens of triggers and attributes.
Our security platform uses a multi-layered approach to threat detection, combining network, endpoint, and user behavior data.

variable_elements.primary_metric: A primary optimization variable (e.g., Time since visit)
variable_elements.secondary_metric: A secondary, independent optimization variable (e.g., Geographic proximity)
variable_elements.comparison_basis: Illustration of internal logic and rules

must_have: At least two independent variables your system uses for optimization (e.g., location, time, user segment)
A quantifiable output that is affected by these variables (e.g., price, score, bid)
A large number representing the total combinatorial possibilities or 'expressiveness' of the system
data_requirements.data_shape_needed: Needs to show a logical, rule-based relationship (e.g., a decay curve, a tiered structure) for at least two different variables.
data_requirements.minimum_data_points: 2+ optimization variables, with 3-5+ rules or data points for each to illustrate the logic.

ideal_for: Proving your technology is more sophisticated than competitors'.
Justifying a premium price point by showing the complexity that drives ROI.
Explaining your 'secret sauce' or technical moat to investors or technical buyers.
Illustrating how your platform delivers superior results (e.g., cost savings, higher conversion).
In a product deep-dive section of a presentation.
avoid_when: Your product's value proposition is simplicity, not power and complexity.
You are presenting to a non-technical audience that would be confused by the details.
You cannot clearly articulate or visualize the variables your system uses.

records.title: TTD + Agency reduced client's booking costs by half.

records.core_message: Our comprehensive platform consolidates spending from multiple point solutions, allowing us to capture a much larger share of our customers' total budget.

shows.specific_content: A diagram illustrating a hypothetical media plan budget allocation. An 'Agency' budget is shown fragmented across multiple vendors: an 'Agency Trading Desk' (20%), and various other solution companies (4x 10%). The diagram visually implies that The Trade Desk's platform can consolidate or replace all these disparate functions, allowing it to capture a much larger portion of the budget, represented by a 40% block.
shows.data_points_shown: Illustrative budget allocation percentages: 40% (The Trade Desk potential), 20% (Agency Trading Desk), 10% (Marketing Solution), 10% (Managed Service), 10% (Ad Software), 10% (Data/Tech).

records.abstract_pattern: This pattern illustrates how a comprehensive platform can consolidate a fragmented market of point solutions. It visually represents a customer's total spend, breaking it down into portions allocated to various single-function vendors. The slide then asserts that the company's platform can absorb the functions (and thus the budget) of these disparate vendors, leading to a significantly larger share of the customer's wallet. This is a classic 'platform vs. point solution' or 'vendor consolidation' argument, used to demonstrate a large, addressable market opportunity within an existing customer base and justify an expansion strategy.
works_for: Our security platform replaces 5 different security tools, consolidating our customer's security budget.
By using our all-in-one HR suite, companies can eliminate separate payroll, benefits, and recruiting software.
Our marketing automation platform integrates email, social, and analytics, capturing budget previously spent on three separate tools.
Our developer platform combines code hosting, CI/CD, and monitoring, consolidating spend on multiple DevOps tools.
Our financial OS for SMBs replaces separate invoicing, expense tracking, and banking software.
We are the central nervous system for the modern data stack, consolidating spend across ingestion, transformation, and BI.
Our communications platform unifies voice, video, and messaging, replacing multiple niche apps.

variable_elements.primary_metric: Share of customer budget / wallet
variable_elements.secondary_metric: Number of point solutions or competitor categories
variable_elements.comparison_basis: Own platform vs. a fragmented set of competitor types/point solutions

must_have: An understanding of a typical customer's budget allocation in your domain
A list of competitor categories or specific point solutions that customers use
A credible narrative for why your platform can replace or subsume the functions of those other solutions
data_requirements.data_shape_needed: Needs a breakdown of a whole (e.g., 100% of a budget) into multiple parts, where the company can claim to consolidate several of those parts.
data_requirements.minimum_data_points: 3-5 competitor categories or point solutions to illustrate fragmentation.

ideal_for: Explaining a 'land and expand' strategy to investors.
Justifying a higher valuation based on capturing more share of wallet from existing customers.
Demonstrating a competitive moat against smaller, single-function point solutions.
When selling a platform vision, not just a product feature.
To show customers the TCO (Total Cost of Ownership) and simplification benefits of your platform.
Arguing that your addressable market is larger than it appears because you can expand within accounts.
avoid_when: You are a point solution yourself and don't have a credible platform story.
Your product only integrates with other tools, it doesn't replace them.
Your customers strongly prefer a 'best-of-breed' approach and resist vendor consolidation.

records.title: Our platform approach wins more of the budget.

records.core_message: We are proactively solving a major industry-wide problem (identity) by creating and championing an open, collaborative, non-proprietary standard, establishing our leadership and building a durable moat.

shows.specific_content: A title slide for 'Unified ID 2.0' with the subtitle 'The what and why...'. It lists five key attributes and actions related to this initiative, including collaboration, open-sourcing the technology, dedicating resources, its philosophical underpinning, and its non-proprietary nature.

records.abstract_pattern: Any company can use this pattern to introduce a major strategic initiative it is leading to solve an industry-wide problem. The slide frames the company as a benevolent leader, creating an open, non-proprietary standard or technology that benefits the entire ecosystem. This approach builds a powerful moat by positioning the company's solution as the de facto standard, creating network effects and making the company an indispensable partner, contrasting with closed, proprietary alternatives.
works_for: We are solving the AI security problem by creating an open-source framework for the whole industry.
Our company led the consortium to define the new standard for interoperable IoT devices.
To accelerate EV adoption, we've open-sourced our charging connector design and patents.
We are tackling data privacy with a free, open protocol for decentralized identity that anyone can use.
Our contribution of a core technology to a major foundation is making cloud computing more secure for everyone.
We built and are giving away a developer toolkit to help the entire industry transition to a new API standard.
We are creating the 'rails' for the next generation of decentralized finance by building an open protocol.

variable_elements.primary_metric: The name of the strategic initiative, standard, or open-source project.
variable_elements.secondary_metric: The industry-wide problem being solved (e.g., cookie deprecation, lack of interoperability).
variable_elements.time_dimension: Snapshot of the initiative's purpose and characteristics.
variable_elements.comparison_basis: Implicitly compares an open, collaborative approach against closed, proprietary alternatives.

must_have: A clearly defined strategic initiative or project name
A description of the industry-wide problem it solves
A list of actions taken to create/support it (e.g., 'built technology', 'formed a partnership')
A statement on its philosophy (e.g., 'open-source', 'non-proprietary', 'collaborative')
data_requirements.data_shape_needed: qualitative_list
data_requirements.minimum_data_points: 3-5 key attributes or actions that define the initiative

ideal_for: Explaining how you are future-proofing your business against a major industry shift.
Establishing your company as an industry thought leader, not just a participant.
Building the case for a moat based on ecosystem adoption and network effects.
Differentiating an open, collaborative strategy from competitors' 'walled garden' approaches.
Rallying partners and the broader ecosystem around a standard you are championing.
Justifying significant R&D or strategic investment that doesn't have an immediate, direct ROI.
avoid_when: If your solution is purely proprietary and you have no ecosystem story.
If you are an early-stage startup without the credibility to lead an industry-wide initiative.
When your core strategy is to lock customers into a closed ecosystem.

records.core_message: This slide introduces the upcoming section of the presentation, which will detail the key factors and strategies that are expected to fuel the company's future growth.

data_requirements.minimum_data_points: 1 section title

Introducing the key pillars of your strategy (e.g., growth, product, market).
Setting the agenda for the next few slides to improve audience comprehension.
Signaling a shift in focus, for example from 'what we've done' to 'where we're going'.
Reinforcing the brand while introducing a new section.

records.title: CTV and TTD

records.core_message: The market for ad-supported content is massive and durable because the alternative (ad-free subscription models) is fundamentally too expensive for the majority of consumers.

shows.specific_content: A background image of a person watching TV from behind, with an overlaid text box stating 'The future of TV is ad funded. The cost of no ads is too great for most consumers.' A small footnote cites the 'Leichtman Research Group, Inc.'
shows.data_points_shown: A qualitative assertion about the economic unsustainability of ad-free models for mass-market consumers. No quantitative data is displayed.

records.abstract_pattern: This is a 'Market Thesis' slide. It establishes a foundational belief about an industry's future by making a strong, declarative statement about a macro trend or fundamental customer behavior. It often uses an evocative image to set the scene and may subtly cite an external authority to add weight. Any company can use this pattern to frame the entire market opportunity, asserting a forward-looking truth as an inevitable reality, which in turn makes the company's solution a logical and necessary consequence.
works_for: The future of enterprise software is composable and API-first.
Every company will eventually become a fintech company.
The next generation of consumers demands fractional ownership of assets.
The true cost of carbon will be priced into every supply chain.
The future of healthcare is moving from the hospital to the home.
Local commerce is the next trillion-dollar e-commerce wave.
Data privacy is shifting from a feature to a fundamental consumer right.

variable_elements.primary_metric: Core Assertion: A declarative statement about a future state or fundamental truth.
variable_elements.secondary_metric: Supporting Rationale: The underlying reason (e.g., cost, convenience, technology shift) for the assertion.
variable_elements.comparison_basis: An implicit or explicit comparison between two models or futures (e.g., ad-funded vs. subscription, centralized vs. decentralized).

must_have: A strong, defensible point of view or thesis about your market's future.
A clear, concise rationale explaining why this future is inevitable.
data_requirements.data_shape_needed: needs a strong, forward-looking, and often contrarian opinion
data_requirements.minimum_data_points: One core assertion and one supporting reason.

ideal_for: Opening a presentation to establish the 'why now' and the scale of the opportunity.
Justifying your Total Addressable Market (TAM) with a qualitative, top-down argument.
Making a visionary statement to position your company as a thought leader.
Explaining the fundamental economic or behavioral shift that your company is built on.
Countering a common misconception about your industry (e.g., that ads are dying).
avoid_when: Your audience expects only quantitative data and performance metrics.
Your core assertion is a generic platitude that doesn't offer a unique insight.
You are deep in the details of a product demo or financial review.

records.title: The future of TV is ad funded.

records.core_message: Advertisers must shift their focus from traditional broadcast TV to Connected TV (CTV) to reach modern audiences, as this is where viewers now are, and we are the leading platform to facilitate this transition.

shows.specific_content: A photograph of a television displaying the user interface for the Sling TV streaming service. The UI shows a grid of TV shows and channels (e.g., Disney, HGTV, Food Network). Text on the slide states 'Our story in CTV is resonating' and 'You are missing out on a core audience if you're only buying broadcast TV.'
shows.data_points_shown: No quantitative data is shown. The slide uses a qualitative claim and a representative image of a CTV platform to illustrate a market shift.

records.abstract_pattern: This pattern establishes a major, irreversible shift in customer behavior by contrasting an obsolete 'Old Way' with a dominant 'New Way'. It uses a compelling, tangible image of the 'New Way' in action to make the trend feel real and current. The core message is framed as a direct warning to the audience, creating a fear of missing out (FOMO) and positioning the company as the essential guide for navigating this new landscape.
works_for: You're losing customers if your checkout is only on desktop, not mobile.
Your sales team is flying blind if they're still using spreadsheets instead of a modern CRM.
Companies relying on on-premise servers are falling behind in agility and cost-efficiency.
If you're not using AI in your customer support, you're delivering a subpar experience.
Brands that only market on social media are missing the high-intent audience on search.
Retailers without an omnichannel strategy are becoming irrelevant to modern shoppers.
Your team's productivity is capped if they're communicating in email instead of a real-time collaboration hub.

variable_elements.primary_metric: The 'Old Way' of operating (e.g., buying broadcast TV ads)
variable_elements.secondary_metric: The 'New Way' of operating (e.g., buying CTV ads)
variable_elements.time_dimension: Implicit present/future trend (the shift is happening now)
variable_elements.comparison_basis: Obsolete behavior vs. modern behavior

must_have: A clear understanding of a major industry or behavioral shift
A strong, evocative image representing the 'new way'
A compelling, concise statement that creates urgency or FOMO
data_requirements.data_shape_needed: Qualitative narrative; needs a clear 'before and after' or 'old vs. new' dichotomy.
data_requirements.minimum_data_points: Not applicable; this is a qualitative, narrative-driven slide.

ideal_for: Establishing the 'Why now?' for your company or product.
Creating a sense of urgency for potential customers to adopt your solution.
Framing the problem your company solves in terms of a major, undeniable industry shift.
Justifying why an old way of doing things is now obsolete or insufficient.
Educating an audience about a new market reality they may not fully grasp.
Making an abstract trend feel tangible and immediate.
avoid_when: The market shift you're describing is not yet obvious or widely accepted.
Your audience is highly analytical and requires hard, quantitative data to be convinced.
Your audience is already an expert on the trend and needs to see solution details, not problem framing.

records.title: Our story in CTV is resonating

records.core_message: Our platform has achieved massive, market-leading scale, reaching a significant majority of US households and an even larger number of high-value connected TV devices.

It often uses a simple, declarative title to state the conclusion (e.g., 'Our scale is massive') and then provides the numbers as undeniable proof. This is used to establish market leadership, credibility, and the sheer size of the opportunity the company represents for its customers or partners. The visual design emphasizes the magnitude of the numbers, making them the focal point of the slide.
works_for: We process over 500 billion transactions daily.
Our platform connects 80% of all US hospital systems.
Our creator community has produced over 1 billion pieces of content.
We have mapped over 95% of the world's supply chains.
Our marketplace has over 200 million active monthly users.
Our API powers 1 in 3 e-commerce checkouts online.
Our security software protects over 500 million endpoints globally.
Our data platform ingests over 10 petabytes of new data each day.

variable_elements.primary_metric: A measure of breadth or penetration (e.g., households, users, customers).
variable_elements.secondary_metric: A measure of depth or strategic focus (e.g., devices, transactions, high-value segments).
variable_elements.comparison_basis: Implicitly compared to the total market size (e.g., 90M households vs. ~130M total US households).

must_have: A primary metric quantifying reach or scale (e.g., user count, household penetration, customer count)
A secondary, related metric that adds another dimension to the scale story (optional but powerful)
data_requirements.data_shape_needed: needs large, impressive absolute numbers
data_requirements.minimum_data_points: 1-2 key metrics

ideal_for: Establishing your company as a dominant player in the market.
Quantifying the size of your network or user base for investors or partners.
Showing potential customers the massive audience they can access through your platform.
Making a simple, powerful statement about your scale early in a presentation.
Justifying a high valuation based on market penetration and reach.

A unit cost for your new method (typically higher)

A qualitative explanation for the old method's inefficiency

Differentiating your high-end product in a commoditized market.

records.core_message: Our business is not just growing; it's fundamentally sound, delivering substantial and sustained profitability over many years, as shown by both adjusted and GAAP metrics.

shows.specific_content: Two side-by-side quarterly bar charts from Q2 2016 to Q1 2022. The left chart shows 'Adj. EBITDA' in millions, with a strong, consistent upward trend. The right chart shows 'GAAP Net Income' in millions, which also trends upward but with more volatility, including a few negative quarters.
shows.data_points_shown: Quarterly Adj. EBITDA from $15.7M to a peak of $191.5M. Quarterly GAAP Net Income from -$4.6M to a peak of $151.9M. The time period covers 24 quarters.

records.abstract_pattern: This pattern demonstrates long-term financial strength by presenting key profitability metrics over an extended time series. It typically uses two related charts: a non-GAAP metric (like Adjusted EBITDA) to show core operational performance, and a GAAP metric (like Net Income) to provide financial rigor and transparency. The overall narrative is one of sustained, and often growing, profitability, proving the business model is not just a growth story but a fundamentally sound and durable enterprise. Any mature company can use this to prove its financial viability and operational excellence to investors.
works_for: We have a proven track record of generating significant free cash flow.
Our business model is not only scalable but also highly profitable.
We have been profitable on a non-GAAP basis for 12 consecutive quarters.
Our operating margin has consistently expanded over the past four years.
Unlike our competitors, we have achieved rapid growth without sacrificing profitability.
Our shift to a new business model has dramatically improved our recurring profit.
We have a clear and demonstrated path to sustained GAAP profitability.

variable_elements.primary_metric: A primary profitability metric (e.g., Adjusted EBITDA, Operating Income, Free Cash Flow)
variable_elements.secondary_metric: A secondary, often more stringent, profitability metric (e.g., GAAP Net Income)
variable_elements.comparison_basis: Self over time

must_have: Time-series data for at least one key profitability metric (e.g., Adj. EBITDA, Net Income, Operating Income)
Quarterly or annual financial records
data_requirements.data_shape_needed: needs upward trend
data_requirements.minimum_data_points: 8+ quarters to show a multi-year trend

ideal_for: Proving to late-stage or public market investors that the company is a sound investment.
Differentiating from high-growth, cash-burning competitors.
Showing the financial maturity and stability of the business model.
In an IPO roadshow or investor day presentation to build confidence.
Justifying a premium valuation based on strong fundamentals.
Demonstrating that growth and profitability are not mutually exclusive.
avoid_when: When the company is pre-profitability or has inconsistent/declining profits.
When the primary narrative is about user growth or market capture, not financial performance.
When presenting to an early-stage audience focused solely on vision and TAM.

records.title: ...delivering substantial profitability

records.core_message: Our company is a uniquely compelling investment because we combine rapid growth, long-term profitability, a massive market, a sticky business model, and superior technology.

shows.specific_content: A numbered list of seven key investment highlights, covering revenue growth (43% y/y), revenue predictability (95%+ via MSAs), platform type (self-service omnichannel), tech advantage, market size (massive TAM), business model alignment (buy-side only), and long-term profitability (GAAP profitable since 2013). It concludes with the statement 'TTD is an investment in the whole internet.'
shows.data_points_shown: Q1 revenue grew 43% y/y; 95%+ of spend through MSAs; GAAP profitable since 2013.

records.abstract_pattern: This is a 'reasons to believe' or 'investment thesis' summary slide. It consolidates the most powerful arguments from different aspects of the business—such as growth, profitability, market size, and competitive moat—into a single, digestible list. Any company can use this pattern near the end of a presentation to recap the core value proposition and leave the audience with a clear, strong impression. The pattern works by stacking multiple, distinct proof points to create an overwhelming sense of credibility and a comprehensive case for success.
works_for: To summarize, we have a unique combination of rapid growth and strong profitability.
Here are the five reasons we will win our market: our team, our tech, our traction, our timing, and our total addressable market.
Our company is a durable, long-term business with a strong moat and multiple growth vectors.
We are the clear market leader due to our superior technology, sticky customer base, and scalable business model.
Our platform is the best choice because it's the most powerful, the most open, and has a proven track record of delivering ROI.
We have strong product-market fit, a scalable go-to-market engine, and a clear path to $100M ARR.
Our investment case is built on three pillars: a massive market, a differentiated product, and world-class unit economics.

variable_elements.primary_metric: A list of qualitative and quantitative proof points
variable_elements.comparison_basis: Self-referential summary of company strengths

must_have: A set of 5-7 strong, distinct proof points across different business areas (e.g., a growth metric, a profitability metric, a market size claim, a product advantage claim, a business model claim)
data_requirements.data_shape_needed: Needs a collection of impressive, standalone facts or claims. The power comes from the combination, not a trend in a single dataset.
data_requirements.minimum_data_points: 5-7 distinct highlight points

ideal_for: Summarizing the core investment thesis at the end of an investor pitch.
Providing a 'cheat sheet' of the company's strongest arguments before Q&A.
When you have multiple, distinct strengths (e.g., growth, profitability, tech) that don't fit on a single chart.
Reinforcing the key takeaways from the entire presentation.
As an opening slide to frame the discussion for a sophisticated audience.
Justifying a high valuation by showcasing a rare combination of positive attributes.
avoid_when: You are an early-stage company without multiple, strong proof points across different categories.
Your story is focused on a single, powerful metric that is better shown visually on its own.
The presentation is a deep dive into a single topic (e.g., product demo, technology architecture).
